name: Lemon Amaretti Biscotti (gluten-free almond cookies)

source.author: Recipe app screenshot
source.notes: Analyzed from an app screenshot. Recipe stated for 25 servings; user confirmed the batch made ~25 cookies, so per-serving = per-cookie. Steps 3–6 were cut off in the screenshot — standard amaretti are baked ~12–15 min, assumed here (matters for the raw-egg safety note).

steps: Combine egg whites, sugar, ground almonds, lemon zest, salt, vanilla, and lemon juice in a bowl.
(steps 3–6 cut off in screenshot — standard amaretti: shape, roll in powdered sugar, bake ~12–15 min)

him.verdict: A treat, not a goal food. ~120 kcal/cookie but ~12 g of that is added sugar with only 2.7 g protein — a sugar cookie carried by almonds. The one upside is the almond vitamin E (~2.9 mg/cookie, a sperm micro) and healthy fat. On a cut the risk is volume: three cookies is ~360 kcal of mostly sugar. Fine occasionally; keep it to 1–2 and log them.
suggested_mods: Cut the granulated sugar by ~⅓ — amaretti hold together fine with less; drops each cookie toward ~90 kcal / ~8 g sugar
Portion-cap at 1–2 with coffee rather than grazing the batch
Skip the powdered-sugar roll to shave a little more sugar

her_preconception.verdict: A dessert with little prenatal value — high sugar, low nutrient density. Small positives: gluten-free, a little almond vitamin E and magnesium, some folate. Fine as an occasional treat, not a nutrient contributor.
prenatal_highlights: small amounts of vitamin E, magnesium and folate from the almonds

safety_advisories.note: Contains raw egg white — SAFE if fully baked (standard amaretti are). If any are under-baked/chewy-raw in the center, or if dough is tasted, use pasteurized egg whites.
safety_advisories.swap: pasteurized egg whites, or bake fully

suggested_mods: Same sugar cut as above; treat as an occasional indulgence, not a daily item
